title: npm test leaks ~10 GB of real disk per run - ftruncate is NOT sparse on NTFS, and the code under test trashes the file
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-467 (the 1.4 smoke umbrella) - surfaced 2026-08-09 during its live Pod session, listed in tasks/MPI-467/brief.md.

ROOT-CAUSED FROM THE USER'S RECYCLE BIN, 2026-08-09. His C: drive keeps filling and emptying the bin keeps recovering it. The bin held 22 copies of text_encoders/qwen3vl_8b_fp8_scaled.safetensors, ~230 GiB, every one from C:/Users/Fabio/AppData/Local/Temp/mpi462-sweep-<PID>/. Already hit once before: a prior handoff records C: at 99% and 172 GB freed by emptying the bin.

TWO DEFECTS STACK, and neither is sufficient alone.

1. tests/orphan-sweep.test.cjs:38 writes the dep files with fs.ftruncateSync and says so in a comment: "Sparse - the completeness check stats size, so it must match, but this costs no real disk." THAT IS FALSE ON NTFS. ftruncate sets the sparse flag on ext4/APFS; on Windows it fully allocates. MEASURED 2026-08-09: a 512 MiB ftruncate file reports 512M to du and `fsutil sparse queryflag` answers "This file is NOT set as sparse". So the orphan case materialises 10.59 GiB per run, and place(resolveFullUniverse(FLAT)) in the sibling tests writes ~20 GiB more.

2. The code under test TRASHES rather than deletes - routes/downloadManager.js:305 _trash(localPath), logging "sweep: moved to trash". So the test's own fs.rmSync(ROOT) can never reclaim the orphan: the sweep already moved it into the Recycle Bin, where it sits until the user empties it.

The dir is keyed by process.pid, so runs never collide and every run adds another copy. npm test GATES THE RELEASE and runs in CI on every push (.github/workflows/tests.yml), so this fires constantly - on the dev machine it accumulates, on a fresh CI runner it does not, which is exactly why it went unnoticed.

PROOF THESE ARE TEST-GENERATED, NOT DOWNLOADS: the bin holds two size groups, 10.59 GiB and 9.86 GiB. DEPS['boogu-qwen3vl-8b-clip'].size reads 9.86GB today, so the older entries were written when the declaration said 10.59GB. The files track the DECLARED size, which a real download never would.

FIX DIRECTION: the completeness check only stats size, so the file needs the right st_size and no real bytes. Either set the NTFS sparse flag explicitly before truncating, or stop using a multi-GB dep as the orphan fixture. Do NOT weaken the assertion that the sweep really removed the file - that is the whole point of MPI-462. Fixing the permanent-delete card removes the PERSISTENCE but not the per-run write cost; both halves want doing.
